newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea zinc demand up on talk of price rise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea zinc demand up on talk of price rise.

text.p: South Korea zinc demand has picked up this week on talk that Korea Zinc Co may raise its selling prices by 100 won a kilo in April in line with a rise on the London market, traders said.
They said dwindling zinc inventories had contributed.
"Local consumers' zinc inventory has recently fallen to a level for just one month's use from the previous two-month level," a trader said.
Despite strong demand, zinc selling prices had hovered flat at 1.187 million won per tonne this week.
Korea Zinc is South Korea's largest zinc and lead producer.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery had eased slightly to $85-$90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices, from $90 a week ago, traders added.
Domestic aluminium prices were unchanged at 1.53 million won a tonne over the past week.
But traders said there had been some aluminium offers at below 1.5 million won in the domestic physical market.
LG Cable and Machinery Ltd bought 500 tonnes of aluminium from LG Metals Corp at below 1.5 million won, they said.

They said monthly sales of four major domestic aluminium rolling mills fell in February to 18,282 tonnes from 18,704 a month earlier. Exports of aluminium roll products dropped to 4,637 tonnes from 5,141 in January.
Copper prices had been flat at 2.297 million won per tonne over the past week and lead prices had remained unchanged at 703,000 won.
They said LG Metals copper output in February totalled 20,000 tonnes, down from 21,100 in January.
This was mainly because February had fewer working days than January.
They expected LG output to rise to 23,000 tonnes in March.
